title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: SpaceX swell lifts the Nasdaq while oil churns near $100
conditions.summary: Nasdaq futures edge higher on SpaceX and Super Micro, while the Dow and small caps sit flat to lower. Crude near $100 and a 5.1% 10-year yield keep a lid on the mood.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: S&P 500 futures are up about 0.1% and Nasdaq-100 futures about 0.3% in early, thin trading; Dow futures are near flat and Russell 2000 futures down about 0.2%.
The 10-year Treasury yield is about 5.12% and the 2-year about 4.8%; the dollar index is steady near 101.8.
December WTI crude is up about 2% near $99.90; Brent is around $110. Gold is down 0.2% near $4,134.
Bitcoin is up about 2% near $83,200; the VIX is near 17.5.
Asia was mixed: Japan, South Korea and Australia rose while China and Hong Kong slipped.
Europe is mixed and mostly slightly lower, with the Stoxx 600 and DAX down about 0.1% and the FTSE 100 down about 0.3%.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: No major US economic data today. MBA mortgage applications at 6:00 AM CT, EIA crude inventories at 9:30 AM CT and a 20-year bond auction at 12:00 PM CT.
No Fed speakers are scheduled; CME FedWatch shows about an 85% chance the Fed holds at its October meeting.
Main story: oil near $100 WTI and $110 Brent on Strait of Hormuz tensions as US-Iran talks drag on, keeping the 10-year yield above 5%.
France's unrest has pushed its 10-year yield to the highest since 2002, adding to global bond jitters.

sections.title: Earnings
items: SpaceX beat after Tuesday's close (EPS $0.35, revenue $14.6B vs $12.7B expected); shares up roughly 8% to 10% premarket.
Netflix beat on EPS but missed slightly on revenue and cut ad revenue and free cash flow guidance; shares down about 6%.
Capital One beat on EPS ($6.69 vs $5.50) and revenue; shares up about 3%.
Danaher beat this morning (adjusted EPS $2.11 vs $1.92) and raised its full-year EPS outlook; shares higher premarket.
Also before the open: AT&T, Thermo Fisher, Abbott, Philip Morris and NextEra Energy.
After the close: Tesla, Meta, IBM, Lam Research and Texas Instruments.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: SMCI (Super Micro Computer): +12% to +16% — raised Q1 revenue guidance to $18.5B–$19.5B.
SPCX (SpaceX): about +10% — Q3 beat and first quarterly profit since its IPO; Tesla merger talks.
NFLX (Netflix): about -6% — weak Q4 revenue outlook and lower ad revenue guidance.
COF (Capital One): about +3% — Q3 earnings beat.
TSLA (Tesla): about +2% to +3% — ahead of earnings and possible SpaceX merger talks.
LITE (Lumentum): about +4% — Jefferies raised its price target to $1,250.
CRWV, NVDA, INTC (CoreWeave, Nvidia, Intel): +2% to +4% — Musk dismissed fears of an AI compute glut.

sections.title: Business News
items: Salesforce agreed to buy Braze for about $5.66 billion, or $47.50 a share in cash.
Nvidia signed a physical-AI declaration of intent with Germany and named German startups it will back.
France imposed curfews in major cities after rioting; its 10-year yield hit the highest since 2002.
Saudi Arabia canceled its Future Investment Initiative conference after attacks near Riyadh.
Schneider Electric is raising about €6 billion in new equity to help fund its $22.6 billion PTC deal.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 8:30 AM CT open: whether the SpaceX and Super Micro rally holds and lifts the Nasdaq.
9:30 AM CT EIA crude report and the noon CT 20-year auction, with oil near $100 and the 10-year above 5%.
After the close: Tesla and Meta kick off Big Tech earnings.
